name: a resume takes the second-fetch reload path
why: startFetchingProcess() answers a second press with window.location.reload(), and nothing re-presses afterwards. A resume that took that door would destroy the very rows it exists to keep and leave the user on a bare page. This is the guard whose absence stalled the first five runs of this spec.

name: the row accumulators are cleared on a resume after all
why: THE feature. Page 1's rows come from the LIVE document and can never be re-fetched, so clearing the accumulators ends the resumed run at 200 rows while the status line, the request log and the row indices all still look right.

name: the row-index counter is re-zeroed on a resume
why: _mbRowIdxCounter is deliberately left running so resumed rows get FRESH indices. Re-zeroing it yields 300 rows carrying only 200 distinct data-mb-row-idx values — invisible to every row-count and status assertion, and corrupting for every map keyed "rowIdx:colIdx" (expandedCells, _inlineArtSettled, _areaFlagRegionCorrected).

name: the page count is re-probed instead of reused
why: Re-probing costs a request and, worse, puts the High Page Count dialog in front of the user a second time for the same set of pages.

name: the High Page Count dialog is not suppressed on a resume
why: Independent of the maxPage reuse above: even with the count reused, an unguarded dialog re-asks about pages the user already agreed to. The dialog BLOCKS, so the run never finishes.

name: the offer is not cleared at the top of a run
why: _resumeState must be cleared by EVERY run, including a resumed one, or a successful resume leaves a stale offer pointing at a page that has since loaded.

name: the resume point names the wrong page
why: A button that appeared with nextPage 1 would re-fetch from the start, which is the behaviour this feature exists to replace. Pinned as an exact object rather than "a resume state exists".

name: the synthetic click event is missing preventDefault
why: startFetchingProcess() reads e.target and then calls e.preventDefault() and e.stopPropagation(). A bare {target} throws on the second, aborting the resumed run before its first fetch — with no symptom but a run that never finishes.

name: a second press no longer reloads
why: Counter-guard in the other direction: the reload is answered to a SECOND fetch and is deliberately untouched — the resume is exempted from it, not the other way round. Dropping `isLoaded &&` would make every press re-enter, which is the change this branch must not have made.

name: the live-document shortcut is not disabled on a resume
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden. On a resume the render has already replaced the live table with the consolidated one, so `p === currentPageNum` would re-extract this script's own output as page N. It is reachable on a real page — standing on ?page=7 with page 5 failing — but NOT from this fixture, whose currentPageNum is 1 and whose resumed range starts at 2, so p can never equal it. Covering it needs a fixture loaded at a later page than the one that fails.

name: the heading pre-processing runs again on a resume
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden. applyRenameH2ToH3() renames EVERY <h2> and copies its attributes, including the data-mb-injected-h2 marker applyInsertH2() guards on — so a second pass demotes the injected heading and injects another beside it. 18 pageTypes declare both features; artist-events, which this spec uses, declares neither, so no assertion here can see it. Covering it needs a fixture on a *-tags or user-ratings page.
